Gone are the days when we could make fun of AI-generated faces for grotesque errors like mangled cauliflower ears and an inhuman number of teeth. A steady stream of advancements now allow the technology to manufacture faces that look real. A little too real, according to a new study published in Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayPsychologists from the University of Florida recruited over 150 participants—some young (18 to 37), some old (60 to 89)—to find out how their brains responded to seeing faces generated by AI. The participants were shown photos featuring either actual human faces or AI-generated faces and asked to rate how realistic they were on a scale from 1 to 10, all while their brains were scanned by an fMRI machine. Read more: “Creating Fake People is a Terrible Idea”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
